title: Resolution formula for the cotangent base-change adjunct
statement:
Let $A\to C$, $A\to A'$, $f:C\to C'$ and $A'\to C'$ be a commutative square of commutative rings. Let $P_\bullet=P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(C/A)$ and $R_\bullet=P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(C'/A')$ be the standard resolutions, and $t:P_\bullet\to R_\bullet$ the square-induced semilinear map [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. Suppose that $P'_\bullet=P_\bullet\otimes_A A'$, augmented by $p\otimes a'\mapsto f(\epsilon(p))a'$, is a polynomial resolution of $C'$ over $A'$. Put $K=s(\Omega^1_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}C)$, $K'=s(\Omega^1_{P'_\bullet/A'}\otimes_{P'_\bullet}C')$, and $K(R)=s(\Omega^1_{R_\bullet/A'}\otimes_{R_\bullet}C')$, with Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and the nonpositive alternating-complex convention of that coherence node. Suppose $K$ is K-flat with flat $C$-module terms [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Write $Q$ for localization into ordinary-module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $c_K:QK\otimes_C^{\mathbf L}C'\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(K\otimes_C C')$ for the canonical computation map, using derived scalar extension [lem-trf-one-point-derived-ring-identification]. Let $\theta:K\otimes_C C'\to K'$ be the differential chain map $(\mathrm dp\otimes c)\otimes b'\mapsto\mathrm d(p\otimes1)\otimes f(c)b'$ and $u:K\to\operatorname{Res}_f(K\otimes_C C')$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$; tensor products mean [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then $h:P'_\bullet\to R_\bullet$, $h(p\otimes a')=t(p)a'$, is a morphism of augmented polynomial resolutions. If $c_{P'}:QK'\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{C'/A'}$ and $c_R:QK(R)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{C'/A'}$ are the canonical comparisons, then $c_R QK(h)=c_{P'}$, and the standard functoriality morphism $\gamma:L_{C/A}\to\operatorname{Res}_f L_{C'/A'}$ is represented by $c_R QK(h)Q(\theta)Q(u)$, with target maps restricted along $f$. Under the normalized derived extension/restriction adjunction [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] transported to ordinary modules, its adjunct $\beta$ satisfies the equality of morphisms in $D(C')$
$$\beta=c_R QK(h)Q(\theta)c_K=c_{P'}Q(\theta)c_K.$$
Neither invertibility of $\theta$ nor the derived-multiplication hypothesis is assumed in this assertion. Flat modules are as in [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and simplicial objects and their morphisms are as in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object].

proof.text: Construct $h$ degreewise. Since $t_n$ is semilinear over $A\to A'$, the assignment $p\otimes a'\mapsto t_n(p)a'$ is balanced: $t_n(ap)a'=t_n(p)\alpha(a)a'$. It is additive, multiplicative and unital, hence gives an $A'$-algebra map $P_n\otimes_A A'\to R_n$. For every simplicial operator $\sigma$, $R(\sigma)h_n(p\otimes a')=t_m(P(\sigma)p)a'=h_m(P(\sigma)p\otimes a')$, using that $t$ is simplicial. The target augmentation sends $h_n(p\otimes a')$ to $f(\epsilon(p))a'$, the specified source augmentation. Thus $h$ is an augmented resolution morphism; both endpoints are polynomial resolutions by the hypotheses and the standard-resolution assertion.

proof.text: Apply the naturality of the canonical comparisons in [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] over the single base ring $A'$, with target algebra $C'$, to the augmented resolution morphism $h:P'_\bullet\to R_\bullet$ from Step 1. It gives exactly $c_R QK(h)=c_{P'}$. The hypothesis needed here is that $P'_\bullet$ is a polynomial resolution, which is expressly assumed; no flatness of $A\to A'$ or derived-multiplication condition is used.

proof.text: Let $g:K\to\operatorname{Res}_f K(R)$ be the differential map induced by the standard square map $t$. On the generators of its degree $-n$ term it sends $\mathrm dp\otimes c$ to $\mathrm d(t_n(p))\otimes f(c)$. The composite $K(h)\theta u$ sends the same generator successively to $(\mathrm dp\otimes c)\otimes1$, to $\mathrm d(p\otimes1)\otimes f(c)$, and to $\mathrm d(t_n(p))\otimes f(c)$. Differentials are generated by $\mathrm dp$ by their displayed quotient construction, and tensor products by pure tensors, so these maps agree in every degree. They commute with each face map, since applying a ring map and then $\mathrm d$ sends $p$ to the differential of its image; therefore they commute with the alternating sums, with the same signs. Thus $g=K(h)\theta u$ as chain maps. By the standard functoriality assertion and the canonical comparison to the target, $\gamma=(\operatorname{Res}_f c_R)Q(g)=c_R QK(h)Q(\theta)Q(u)$; $QK=L_{C/A}$ by the standard-resolution definition.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-one-point-derived-ring-identification] to evaluate the normalized sheaf coefficient adjunction of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] on the singleton site at the rings $C$ and $C'$. It preserves the tensor computations, K-flatness, flat terms and the computation isomorphism $c_K$ appearing here. The assumed K-flatness and flat terms of $K$ therefore give the normalized adjunct formula for $g$ of Step 3. Its adjunct is $Q(v)c_K$, where $v:K\otimes_C C'\to K(R)$ sends $x\otimes b'$ to $b' g(x)$. Put $w=K(h)\theta$. This is $C'$-linear and $g(x)=w(x\otimes1)$, so $v(x\otimes b')=b' w(x\otimes1)=w(x\otimes b')$. Equality on pure tensors gives $v=w$. Naturality of the cited adjunction bijection in its target, applied to $c_R:QK(R)\to L_{C'/A'}$, now shows that the adjunct of $\gamma$ is $\beta=c_R QK(h)Q(\theta)c_K$. Substitution of Step 2 gives $\beta=c_{P'}Q(\theta)c_K$. The adjunction has no flat-ring-map or boundedness hypothesis, and the argument never inverts $\theta$.
